title: A blank margin so the stamp fits
allegory: Padding is like taping a blank margin round a page so a 3x3 rubber stamp can be centred on every square, corners included, without hanging off the edge.
map: squares where the stamp can be centred
output positions: L - k + 1 with no padding
a blank margin taped round the page
padding p on every side, so the input becomes L + 2p
blank ink that leaves no mark
the pad constant: 0 for a sum, -inf for a max
the padding that keeps output size equal to input size at stride 1

cap.1: Every time you slide a 3x3 window over a picture, the result comes out a little smaller. Stack a few layers and the picture quietly shrinks away.
cap.2: A 3x3 conv with no padding loses 2 pixels per dimension per layer: 28 becomes 26, then 24. Then x + conv(x) fails, because the shapes no longer match.
cap.3: Unpadded ('valid') convolution maps L to L - k + 1. Eight 3x3 layers eat sixteen pixels, and the mismatch only surfaces where a residual add needs equal shapes.

cap.1: A 3x3 stamp must land fully on the paper, so it can't be centred on an edge square. Tape a blank margin round the page and every square gets stamped.
cap.2: Padding adds a ring of constant values around the input before the kernel slides. With a ring 1 wide, a 3x3 kernel can centre on every original pixel, corners included.
cap.3: Padding p extends each spatial axis by 2p. For odd k at stride 1, p = (k-1)//2 lets every input position be a kernel centre, so output and input shapes agree.

cap.1: Count where the stamp can land: start at the left edge, hop along until you reach the right edge. The margin adds room on both sides.
cap.2: L_out = floor((L + 2p - k) / s) + 1. With k=3, s=1, p=1 you get (L + 2 - 3) + 1 = L. Same size in, same size out.
cap.3: At s=1, p = (k-1)/2 for odd k gives L_out = L. The floor is the second trap: at s=2 an odd size is rounded, so two branches can end up one pixel apart.

cap.1: The ring is just extra squares filled with one constant. The stamp centred on the corner now fits, though five of its nine squares are blank.
cap.2: To implement it, make a bigger tensor full of the pad value, then copy the input into the middle slice. The corner window sees 4 real pixels and 5 padding zeros.
cap.3: Allocate (H + top + bottom, W + left + right) filled with the pad value and write x into [top:top+H, left:left+W]. Border outputs aggregate fewer real inputs.

chapters.name: Which blank?
chapters.verdict: Pick the constant that cannot change the answer.

cap.1: Blank means different things to different tools. For a sum, blank is 0. For 'pick the biggest', blank must be minus infinity, or the margin could win.
cap.2: Zero-pad a convolution: pads times weights add nothing. For max pooling, zeros would beat negative activations, so you pad with -inf instead.
cap.3: Choose the identity element of the reduction: 0 for sums, -inf for max. PyTorch's MaxPool2d pads with implicit negative infinity rather than zeros.

cap.1: Keeping sizes steady is what lets you add a layer's output back onto its input. Later you pad sentences too, with a mask so the filler is ignored.
cap.2: In practice it is one argument: padding=1 or padding='same' on nn.Conv2d. Token batches get padded to one length, with a mask so pads get no attention.
cap.3: Residual adds need shape-preserving blocks. When you batch prompts to read or steer a model, knowing which positions are padding keeps you from reading activations off filler.

coda.title: Start at 28 pixels, stack six layers: find the margin that keeps every bar level
coda.f: range(7).reduce((acc, i) => acc.concat([i === 0 ? 28 : (acc[i-1] <= 0 ? 0 : max(0, floor((acc[i-1] + 2*p - k)/s) + 1))]), [])

readouts.label: x + conv(x)?
readouts.f: floor((28 + 2*p - k)/s) + 1 === 28 ? 'works: shapes match' : 'fails: shapes differ'

readouts.label: padding that keeps size at stride 1

caption.1: Set padding to 0 and watch the picture shrink layer by layer. Then find the padding that keeps every bar level, for each kernel size.
caption.2: At stride 1 the bars go flat at p = (k-1)/2: 1 for a 3x3, 2 for a 5x5. Now try stride 2: the size roughly halves each layer, which is what a downsample wants.
caption.3: Each bar applies floor((L + 2p - k)/s) + 1. Over-pad and the map grows by 2p - k + 1 per layer. At s=2 the floor decides odd sizes: 7 goes to 4 with p=1, k=3.

where_else: Residual blocks: shape-preserving convolutions are what make x + conv(x) legal
Causal 1D convolutions, which pad only on the left so no output peeks at the future
Token batches padded to one length, with an attention mask so the pads are ignored
Max pooling, which pads with minus infinity so the margin never wins

hamming.what: A ring of constant values added round an input so a sliding window can reach its edges.
hamming.when: Whenever you slide a window (convolution, pooling) and want to control the output size, most often to keep it unchanged.
hamming.why: Without it every layer shrinks the map and residual adds break; a constant that is neutral for the operation keeps the margin from changing the answer.

object.title: The coverage tray
object.subtitle: Each bar shows how much of the stamp lands on real pixels rather than on the blank margin.

cap.1: No margin: only the middle 6x6 squares can hold the stamp, so the output shrinks. Every surviving output sees nine real pixels.
cap.2: Valid convolution on an 8x8 input: 6x6 out, and every window is fully real.
cap.3: p=0, k=3: L_out = L - 2. Uniform coverage, lost border.

cap.1: Tape on a margin one square wide: now all 8x8 squares get an output, but the corners only see four real pixels.
cap.2: Same-size padding for a 3x3 gives 8x8 out. Corner windows are 4/9 real, edges 6/9, the interior 9/9.
cap.3: p = (k-1)/2 preserves shape at the cost of boundary outputs that aggregate fewer real inputs.

cap.1: From above you can see the rim: a lower ring round the edge where the stamp hangs over the margin.
cap.2: The low rim is the edge effect: border outputs are computed partly from padding constants.
cap.3: Border outputs sum over fewer real terms, so a network can tell where the edge of the image is.

cap.1: A bigger 5x5 stamp needs a margin two squares wide to keep the size. The rim gets wider and the corners see even less.
cap.2: k=5 needs p=2 to preserve size. Corner windows are only 9/25 real.
cap.3: For odd k at stride 1, p = (k-1)/2, and the partly-real band is (k-1)/2 wide on each side.

cap.1: Take the margin away with the big stamp and the output shrinks to 4x4: four pixels lost per dimension in one layer.
cap.2: No padding, k=5: 8 becomes 4. Stack a second one and nothing is left.
cap.3: Valid k=5 maps L to L - 4, so two layers take 8 to 0. Per-layer shape bookkeeping is not optional.

predict.q: A 3x3 conv, stride 1, no padding, on a 28x28 image. What size comes out?
predict.why: L - k + 1 = 28 - 3 + 1 = 26. It takes p = 1 to keep 28.

predict.q: You pad a max-pool with zeros, and all the activations are negative. What goes wrong?

options.t: Border outputs become 0: the padding wins the max

predict.why: Zero is only neutral for sums. For a max, the neutral blank is minus infinity.

predict.q: Which padding keeps a 5x5 conv at stride 1 the same size?
predict.why: (k-1)/2 = 2 squares on each side gives the stamp room to centre on every pixel.

object.where: Anywhere a window slides: image and audio convolutions, pooling, and token batches padded to one length.
